title: BuildKit Secrets & SSH Forwarding 🤫
description: Securely pass secrets during build time without leaving them in image layers.

slides.title: The Problem with Build‑Time Secrets 🔐
slides.content:
# Never Hardcode Secrets in Dockerfiles

If you `COPY` a private key or `ENV API_KEY=...`, that secret becomes a permanent part of the image layer. Anyone with access to the image can extract it.

Even `ARG` is dangerous because `ARG` values persist in image history (`docker history`).

**Solution:** Docker BuildKit provides **secret mounts** and **SSH agent forwarding** to safely inject secrets only during the build.

slides.title: Enabling BuildKit 🏗️
slides.content:
# BuildKit is the Modern Builder

BuildKit is a new builder backend with many features. It’s enabled by default in Docker Desktop, but on Linux you may need to set:

```bash
export DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1
```
or in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`:
```json
{ "features": { "buildkit": true } }
```

Check with:
```bash
docker buildx version
```
We'll use `docker build` which automatically uses BuildKit if enabled.

slides.title: `--secret` Mount: Injecting a Secret File 📁
slides.content:
# How to Use a Secret During Build

1. Create a secret file on the host (e.g., `token.txt`).
2. In the Dockerfile, mount it temporarily:
   ```dockerfile
   RUN --mount=type=secret,id=mysecret cat /run/secrets/mysecret
   ```
3. At build time, pass the secret:
   ```bash
   docker build --secret id=mysecret,src=token.txt -t myimage .
   ```

The secret is only available in that single `RUN` command and is **not** stored in the final image.

**Example Dockerfile snippet:**
```dockerfile
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=aws_creds \
    AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/run/secrets/aws_creds \
    aws s3 cp s3://mybucket/data ./
```

quizData.question: What happens to a BuildKit secret after the RUN command finishes?

options.text: It is embedded in the image layer
It is removed and not present in the final image

quizData.explanation: BuildKit mounts the secret only for the duration of the RUN command and discards it afterward. No trace remains in the image.

slides.title: SSH Agent Forwarding 🔑
slides.content:
# Access Private Repos Without Copying Keys

Use case: `git clone` private repositories during build.

Dockerfile:
```dockerfile
RUN --mount=type=ssh git clone git@github.com:myorg/private-repo.git
```

Build command:
```bash
docker build --ssh default -t myimage .
```

This forwards the host’s SSH agent socket into the build container temporarily. No SSH keys are baked into the image.

> Requires that the host has `ssh-agent` running and keys added.

slides.title: SSH Build Example 🚀
slides.codeSnippet:
# Dockerfile
FROM alpine
RUN apk add --no-cache git openssh
RUN mkdir -p -m 0700 ~/.ssh && ssh-keyscan github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
RUN --mount=type=ssh git clone git@github.com:myuser/private-config.git /config

# Build
eval $(ssh-agent -s)
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa
docker build --ssh default -t with-config .

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## No More ARG Secrets
Always prefer `--secret` or `--ssh` over passing secrets via `ARG`. ARG values are visible in `docker history`.
